“Understood… and please, just call me Elrond,” Elrond replied. “We are both working under this household, Sir Varrick.”

Varrick’s eyes widened a little, then he straightened his back again. “I apologize,” he said. “My master told me to treat you with more respect. But if you do not mind… Sir Elrond.”

“That is fine,” Elrond said. “No need to worry about formalities with me.”

“Understood, Sir Elrond. I will keep that in mind,” Varrick replied.

Gilbert and Cestina gave Elrond a brief farewell, then turned down another corridor together, their steps matching as they headed off to their lunch. Varrick watched them go for a moment, then started walking, guiding Elrond in the opposite direction.

They moved along a wide corridor that ran out from Gilbert’s office. The floor was the same polished stone as the lobby, and tall windows let in the afternoon light, throwing long, pale shapes across the hallway.

“As you will be living here in the future, Sir Elrond, I will explain the general layout,” Varrick said as they walked side by side. “This floor holds the main rooms for the Alfrost family. The opposite wing houses the important guests and close aides.”

Elrond listened carefully and fixed the information in his mind.

“The staff’s common areas are on the lower floors,” Varrick continued. “Most servants use the back corridors when they move around, so that we do not disturb meetings or visitors.”

As if to prove his words, a maid came from the far end of the hallway with folded linens in her arms, bowed to them in passing, then turned into one of the side passages.

It was different from the frontier, where even noble houses felt closer to big, noisy homes. Everything here had an order that ran under the surface.

They went down a set of stairs, turned along another corridor, and passed several doors with simple plaques beside them. Varrick pointed out a few of them as they went, explaining which rooms were used by long-term staff and which were kept open for future needs.

Finally, he stopped in front of one door near the end of a quieter hallway.

“This will be your room, Sir Elrond,” Varrick said. “It is close enough to the main areas that we can call you when needed, but far enough that you can rest without being disturbed.”

He opened the door and stepped aside.

Elrond walked in.

The room was larger than his S-Class dorm room by a clear margin. A bed stood near one wall, with a clean mattress already in place. A desk and chair faced a window that looked out toward a part of the grounds he had not seen from outside, and a simple wardrobe waited near the corner, its doors still empty inside. There were no decorations yet. The space felt new and unfinished, like a blank page.

“We will begin preparing it immediately,” Varrick explained from the doorway. “If you have any particular requests, please let us know, and we will arrange them.”

Elrond ran his eyes over the room again.

“There is no need to hurry,” he said. “I still have my S-Class dormitory at the Academy, and I will be sleeping there for the time being. You can take your time with this room.”

“I understand,” Varrick replied. “In that case, we will prepare it step by step. When you bring your belongings, we will adjust it to your needs.”

“Thank you,” Elrond said.

Varrick gave a short bow. “If you need anything, please ask any of the staff, or send word through the guard at the gate, Sir Elrond.”

“Understood,” Elrond answered.

He let his eyes run over the room again. The wider bed, the desk by the window, the wardrobe with more space than his current clothes, and the empty shelves all made it clear this was not just a guest room that happened to be open. It was a place House Alfrost was preparing for him to use.

‘So I will live here too,’ he thought. He would start shifting things from the S-Class dorm little by little whenever he had time.

He thought about going back and forth between the Academy and this mansion. There would be Royal Academy lectures as usual, and, whenever something reached House Alfrost, there would also be work here for him. If something happened while he was away, he would not be a bystander. He would be one of the people expected to act, and if he made a mistake it would not only affect him but also the people in this house.

That was another layer of responsibility on top of the one he had already accepted when he shook Gilbert’s hand, and he knew it.

Even so, when he thought about the small home he had left in the frontier and the Astrea name that had always stood far from nobles, he could see how different this future was from the one he had expected. A room in a mansion like this, a direct link to a founding family, and a chance to pull his household up from the edge of the map. None of that had seemed possible when he first arrived in the capital.

“As far as I know, this is more than I ever could have asked for,” he thought.

He was simply grateful for it, and whatever came next, he had no intention of wasting it.

### Chapter 27: 23 - Moving on

#### Scene 1

The day felt like any other.

Emilia’s carriage rolled through the Alfrost gate and stopped in front of the mansion. She stepped down, glanced once at the familiar white walls and neat lines of the building, then walked inside without slowing. This sight had already become part of her routine.

Maids in the entrance hallway noticed her immediately. As she passed, they bowed in the same small way they always did. Emilia returned their greetings with short nods and kept moving toward her room. The sooner she reached her desk, the sooner she could clear the work waiting there.

Eira met her partway down the corridor.

“Welcome back, Lady Emilia,” Eira said as she fell in beside her.

Eira walked beside her and took the bag from her hand, as she always did.

“Is there anything important that I need to attend today, Eira?” Emilia asked.

“No, Lady Emilia. You can take your time to rest,” Eira answered.

In this house, “rest” never really meant lying down and doing nothing. It meant working somewhere more comfortable than the main office.

“Is Father home?” Emilia asked next.

“No. Lord Caelen is still at the palace today,” Eira replied. “Anyway, for lunch, would you like to eat in the dining hall or in your room, Lady Emilia?”

Emilia thought for a moment.

“Bring it to my room,” she said. “I need to finish some documents.”

“Understood,” Eira said with a small nod.

They reached Emilia’s room shortly after. Eira went in ahead, placed the bag neatly on the couch, then stepped back toward the door.

“I will prepare your lunch right away, Lady Emilia,” she said.

Emilia crossed the room to her desk.

The documents for today were already stacked there. Approval forms sat on top, with inventory summaries and short reports from different parts of the mansion underneath. She pulled out her chair, sat down, and picked up the first sheet.

She started working.

Her seal moved from line to line as she gave approvals. When she found something that did not sit right, she stopped and read it twice, then wrote a short note in the margin for later follow-up. Numbers from the inventory lists ran through her head as she checked whether the amounts matched what she remembered from previous days.

After she had worked through several pages, a knock came at the door.

“Please, come in,” Emilia said.

The door opened and Eira entered with a tray in her hands. Today’s lunch was arranged neatly on it. Emilia pushed the papers back just far enough so no soup or sauce would touch them, then began to eat.

Eira stayed in the room while she ate, waiting off to the side. When Emilia finished, she wiped her mouth, set the cutlery on the tray, and Eira stepped forward to take it.

“I will take these back to the kitchen,” Eira said.

“Thank you,” Emilia replied.

Eating in one’s room was not what noble etiquette recommended. Meals were supposed to be taken in the dining hall, especially in a house that carried as much weight as Alfrost. But with Father at the palace, there would be no proper family table today, and Gilbert would most likely end up having lunch with Cestina on his own schedule anyway. If she went to the hall now, she would only sit alone at a long table and wait to see whether her brother appeared.

Here, at least, she could finish her plate and reach for the next document in the same motion.

About an hour passed after lunch.

The stack on her desk grew thinner. Emilia pressed her seal on decisions that were already settled, then made small marks on the edges of reports that needed more than one person’s opinion. Some were meant for Caelen when he returned. Others were things she wanted to ask Gilbert about, in case they brushed up against his work with the crown.

After working through another group of papers, she leaned back in her chair and let her shoulders relax.

Her shoulders were stiff from sitting. She lifted both arms over her head and stretched until the tightness in her back eased a little, then let them fall again. The rest of the papers could wait until later. If she forced herself to keep staring at them now, she would only wear herself out.

“I will take a walk,” she said quietly to herself.

She left the room and stepped into the corridor.

Normally, Liso would have appeared by now, with her usual bright voice and quick steps, insisting on going with her. Liso liked to stay close, especially when Emilia left the main building. Today, Liso was nowhere in sight.

Emilia noticed that small difference and filed it away. Liso could be on a different duty inside the mansion, or finally resting after the last few busy days. Emilia had told her more than once to rest when she could, so she decided not to chase it.

She turned toward the garden.

The air outside was cooler than inside the corridors. The paths that wound through the front garden were lined with trimmed shrubs and flowerbeds. A small fountain sent water up and down, and birds called from the branches of nearby trees. A few servants crossed the farther paths, carrying baskets or tools, but they kept a respectful distance from the main walkways.

Emilia did not aim for any particular corner of the grounds. She just followed the lines of the stone paths and let the cool air settle her.

On one of the inner paths near the mansion, she saw two familiar figures walking toward her from the other side.

“Brother, you haven’t had lunch yet?” Emilia asked when they came close enough.

Gilbert gave her an apologetic smile that did not look very sorry.

“No. I had something to do, so it is a bit late,” he said. At the same time, he glanced at the woman beside him. “Cestina is already sulking, as you can see.”

“I am not sulking,” Cestina protested immediately. “It is just because you did not tell me anything about your meeting.”

Her tone was light, but her cheeks still held a hint of puffed-up annoyance. Emilia had seen this exchange more than a few times by now.

“Huh… always lovey-dovey at any time,” Emilia said with a small sigh. “You two better hurry. It is already past noon.”

“That is right…” Cestina said. She turned to Gilbert. “Let us go, Sir Gilbert. And forgive me, Lady Emilia. I cannot accompany you yet. And it seems Liso is not coming either.”

“That is okay,” Emilia replied. “I just wanted some fresh air.”

They exchanged short waves. Gilbert and Cestina left together for their lunch date.

Emilia turned down another path that led deeper toward the back side of the house.

Here, the garden opened into a wider area. The sound from the front entrance and main road dropped away, and only the breeze and the distant steps of a few staff reached her. Trees were planted in more open lines, and there was more space between the paths. From here, parts of the training grounds and the less decorative side of the mansion were visible.

She walked slowly along the path. She did not need to force herself to think about documents or schedules for a moment. It was enough to listen to the gravel under her shoes and the rustle of leaves in the wind.

Near the back of the mansion, she noticed Varrick standing on another path with someone at his side.

Emilia looked more closely and saw the other person’s face.

It was the face that came back to her every time she remembered the attack on the carriage. The boy who had stepped between them and the assassins on that road, and dragged her, Cestina, and Lisoletelle back from the edge of death in the very moment she had failed to protect them herself.

It was Elrond.

Emilia stopped on the path and watched them.

She could not hear what they were saying, but she could see how they moved. Varrick stood angled toward the gate, ready to lead Elrond that way. Elrond listened, then lifted his right hand in front of his chest, palm facing Varrick.

Varrick stopped. Elrond said something short, and Varrick gave a small nod.

Elrond bowed. Varrick returned the bow at the same depth.

Then they split. Elrond walked back toward the mansion along the stone path that led to the rear entrance near the lobby. Varrick stayed in the garden and turned back toward the inner paths.

Emilia frowned. She watched Elrond until he disappeared behind the corner of the building, then she left her path and walked toward Varrick.

Her shoes crunched lightly on the gravel. Varrick noticed her and straightened. By the time she reached him, he had already bowed.

“Lady Emilia,” he said.

She stopped in front of him.

“Why were you walking with that boy, Varrick?” Emilia asked. Her tone was even, but the question left no room to dodge.

“I was showing him around the mansion, Lady Emilia,” Varrick answered.

She narrowed her eyes.

“Showing him around,” she repeated. “Why?”

Varrick lowered his gaze, then spoke.

“Because he will start living in this mansion as soon as possible, Lady Emilia,” he said. “I was ordered to guide him.”

Emilia stopped. No one had said a word to her about him living here.

“Living… here?” she muttered.

Until now, Elrond had only been the boy who had saved Cestina and Liso when she failed to protect them, and the classmate whose strength made her failure hurt more whenever she remembered it. No one had told her that boy would live under the same roof.

Her next words came out sharper.

“What do you mean he will live here?” Emilia asked. “No one told me anything about that. What is going on, Varrick?”

She pressed her palm flat against the side of her skirt.

Varrick bowed his head a little lower.

“As far as I know, he will work here,” he replied. “But my information may not be complete. I believe it would be better for Lady Emilia to ask Lord Gilbert directly. He is the one who ordered me to show Sir Ast—Sir Elrond around the mansion. I apologize that I cannot say more.”

“No, it is fine,” she said. “Thank you, Varrick. I will ask Brother myself.”

Varrick straightened.

“Understood, Lady Emilia,” he said.

She gave him a small nod in return and turned back toward the mansion.

On the way to the rear entrance, her thoughts stayed on what Varrick had said. Gilbert had received that kind of information and given orders without a word to her. It was not against any rule, but it was not something she liked to discover by chance in the garden.

She went back into the mansion and turned toward the office wing. Gilbert’s office at the corner was dark and closed.

She opened the door. The desk still held its usual reports, but the chair behind it was empty.

Emilia went in and sat on the couch where she usually reviewed documents with Gilbert. Today her hands were empty.

The latch moved not long after Emilia sat down.

The door opened, and Gilbert and Cestina stepped inside together. Gilbert’s hand was still on the handle when he stopped. Cestina’s smile faded into a small, surprised “oh” when she saw Emilia on the couch.

“Emilia? Why are you here?” Gilbert asked. His voice was light, but his eyes swept the room before coming back to her.

“Please explain to me, dear Brother,” she said.

Emilia looked straight at him and folded her arms across her chest.

“Explain… what?” he asked. Then his expression shifted as the thought caught up. “Ah. This is about Elrond, I assume.”

“Yes,” Emilia said. “Why is he suddenly working here?”

She folded her arms across her chest. It was not something she did often in front of him.

“What is the matter, Emilia? Is it not a good thing?” Gilbert asked. “He helped us, after all.”

“That is right,” Cestina said, moving a little closer to his side. “And you are acting very strange whenever it is about Elrond, Lady Emilia. What is bothering you?”

The question landed where Emilia did not want it.

To Emilia, Elrond was still the boy who had stepped between them and the assassins on that road when she failed to protect Cestina and Liso. At the Academy, standing there while Cestina went over to speak with him had already pushed that same failure back into her mind. The idea of Elrond living here made Emilia feel insecure and even a little envious. But she decided to accept that truth without telling anyone the real reason. She promised herself she would get better and stronger.

“Nothing is bothering me,” she said. “I simply feel uneasy that someone my age has suddenly moved in and started working here. It is… abrupt.”

Cestina did not look convinced.

At the academy a few days ago, and now in this room, Emilia’s way of dealing with Elrond was almost the same. She kept some distance from him, as if she were avoiding him on purpose, even though she never said anything bad about him. Cestina could see that. Gilbert, however, did not chase it.

He let the question go and moved to the point instead.

“I asked him to live here as a guardian,” he said. “After what he did saving you and Cestina, leaving him outside as if nothing happened would be strange. This is our way of giving thanks, and of giving him a proper position.”

Emilia’s expression tightened.

“A guardian,” she repeated. “That is no small role, Brother. Is it not too sudden to hand such a post to someone we barely know, even if he has done much for us?”

“It is not as if I am placing the household key in his hand on the first day,” Gilbert said. “He will be under my eye, and under the house rules. That is more secure than leaving him as a wandering talent.”

Emilia did not look fully convinced.

“Have you at least spoken with Father about this?” she asked. “About taking him in and giving him that post?”

Gilbert shook his head once.

““Not yet,” he said. “But there is no need to worry. Even though I have not asked Father, he will agree with me when I report it.” His gaze sharpened just a little. “Are you looking down on my judgment?”

He said it gently. The words themselves left no room to step past.

When Gilbert said that, Emilia felt she had lost. Gilbert was a genius. He always thought several steps ahead, and she knew that better than anyone. If he said he had already thought this through, then there was likely a bigger reason behind his decision that she could not see yet. Even so, she still wanted to understand it.

“…No,” she said. “I apologize if it sounded that way. That was not my intent, dear Brother.”

She lowered her arms, but did not drop her gaze.

“But I still want to know the real reason you did this,” she added. “Not just that it is thanks or convenience.”

“It is simple,” Gilbert replied with a slight smile. “I do not want Elrond to fall into the hands of the wrong person. There are many people who would want a talent like his for themselves. That is why I took him first.”

Cestina’s shoulders relaxed at that. It fit what she knew of Gilbert.

Emilia looked between the two of them.

“Understood,” she said at last. “Then I will follow your judgment, dear Brother. I hope he will become a good presence in this house.”

Those were the words she could say out loud.

Even as she accepted his decision, the unsettled feeling in her did not disappear. She knew she would have to deal with it sooner or later. Elrond would be here, in this mansion, every day. She would see him again and again under the same roof.

The talk in the office ended there.

Gilbert gave a small nod, as if closing the subject.

“In that case, I will let the staff about this,” he said. “You can leave the rest to me.”

“Yes,” Emilia replied.

Cestina looked as if she wanted to say something more to Emilia, but when she saw the look on Emilia’s face, she only bowed.

“Then I will excuse myself for today, Lady Emilia,” Cestina said. “There are still things I must do before evening.”

“Of course,” Emilia said. “Thank you for your time.”

They traded short bows and farewells. Then Emilia stepped out of Gilbert’s room.

The corridor outside felt a little cooler.

She stopped in front of the door and let herself think the words she had already decided on inside the room.

'I need to settle this. I cannot let this feeling linger all the time. I need to get stronger.'

She held that thought for a moment, then turned back toward her own room. Her documents were still waiting on her desk. For now, she would go back to them.

.........

With the mansion tour finished, Elrond walked out through the Alfrost gate and headed back toward the Royal Academy.

On the way, he thought again about the decision he had just made. Saying yes to Gilbert’s offer to take him into the Alfrost mansion as a guardian was going to change his life by a lot. It would raise him from a frontier-born commoner into someone directly tied to a noble house.

But how would he be treated in the classroom? Would he be able to disclose it to anyone else?

He still could not answer that. For safety, he decided to let things settle and stay silent about it, at least until Gilbert chose to say something first.

By the time he reached that decision, the Academy was already in sight.

He passed through the gate and walked to the S-Class dormitory. When he opened the door to his room, the magnificent space greeted him again. Even now, it still felt like a place he should not have been able to afford, and yet it was his.

He hesitated at the door, contemplating whether he should leave this dorm at all. It felt like a waste to abandon such a lavish room. If he left for the Alfrost mansion as Gilbert had said, this room would become nothing more than a place to pass through. He would only come back to pick up the last of his things.

But Gilbert had already told him to move to the Alfrost mansion, and Elrond took that as a mandate. If it was like that, then maybe it was not really a loss. Maybe it was simply an upgrade.

Then another thought struck him.

Living at the Alfrost mansion meant living under the same roof as Emilia Alfrost.

Elrond thought carefully. Emilia was a daughter of a Founding family, the kind of person nobles watched. He was still just a commoner from the frontier. If he stayed too close and people began to talk, it would stain Emilia’s name long before it ever touched his.

He did not want that to happen.

So he decided on a simple rule for himself. Unless Gilbert said otherwise, he would not meddle in Emilia’s life. He would move into the mansion, do the work given to him, and keep a respectful distance from the parts of her world that did not need him.

With that thought, he stepped properly into the room and closed the door.

Elrond put the dorm key on the desk and looked over the room in front of him. The decision to move to the Alfrost mansion was already made, so the next step was to start taking his things out of here.

The wardrobe came next. For today, starting with his shirts seemed safest so the room would not change too much at once. Shirts came down one by one and went onto the bed, then each one was folded and placed into a travel case at the edge of the mattress. The space on the rail slowly opened while the shirts in the case slowly stacked up, and that was enough for the first day.

There was no need to hurry, since this was only the first part and the rest could wait. By the time the case was closed, the lamps were still burning inside the room, but the darkness outside the window had thinned into a dull gray. It was almost dawn, so the building was quiet and the corridors stayed empty.

A quick look inside the wardrobe showed that only the shirts were gone, while his uniforms and the rest of his belongings remained in their places. That was how he wanted it, because the plan was to move everything little by little instead of pulling the whole room apart in one night.

With today’s packing finished, the dormitory itself needed to be informed.

Dorm key and acceptance letter in hand, Elrond left the room and walked along the corridor toward the lobby. The hallway was quiet, and pale light from the windows ran along the floor while no other students passed him.

Two women sat at the reception desk, the same receptionists who had once stopped him before the S Class corridor to check his letter and his key. This time, as soon as they noticed him, they straightened in their seats, rose to face him, and greeted him with small, polite smiles.

“Good evening, Sir Astrea. Is there anything we can help with?” one of them asked.

Her tone was even, and the way she called him Sir Astrea showed that they now accepted his position here. Elrond walked up to the counter.

“Uhm… I would like to move out of this dormitory,” he said. “Is there any procedure I should follow?”

He did not add anything else, because talking too much about where he would live next would only sound like bragging.

“Moving out?” the other receptionist repeated. Her brows lifted a little as she looked at him.

“Yes,” Elrond answered. “I am going to move out to my relatives.”

That word was chosen so the matter would stay simple.

“I see… please wait a second,” the first receptionist said.

She turned away and reached under the counter, then searched through some papers before drawing out a single sheet and placing it on the desk in front of him.

“Please fill out this,” she said as she slid the form and an ink pen toward him.

The form only asked for his name, his class, his room number, and the reason he was moving out, which was more relaxed than he had expected for an S Class dorm. Elrond wrote Elrond von Astrea on the first line and S Class on the next, then added his room number and a short line that matched what he had just told them about moving to his relatives. Once the entries were checked, the form went back across the counter.

“Thank you,” the receptionist said.

She looked over the contents and gave a small, satisfied look.

“Understood,” she said. “Please let us know when you are finished packing, then hand the key to us here. And feel free to move back into the dormitory if you need to.”

Her voice made it sound like a rule that already existed for students in this dorm, not a special exception for him in particular. For the Academy, this was just one more move-out request.

Elrond did not plan to come back if he could help it, but it was still better to know that the room would be open if something went wrong at the mansion.

“That is clear,” he said. “Thank you for your help.”

“You are welcome, Sir Astrea,” she replied.

The form went onto a neat pile of other documents, and the receptionist sat down again. The other woman eased her posture and returned to her work. The matter was settled. His choice had gone into the dorm records, and no one had asked where his relatives lived or why he was moving at this time.

Elrond returned to his room and flopped onto his bed. Today had been busier than usual, and a deep sleep sounded like the best way to recover before morning.

The next day at the Academy passed in its usual order. Morning classes came and went, then the afternoon followed without much changing. The same faces filled the same seats. No one stood out. No new trouble appeared.

When the final slot of the day arrived, Elrond headed to Julian again.

The training did not differ much from yesterday on the surface, but Julian’s approach had changed. He did not rely on his divine blessing this time. Instead, he met Elrond head-on and treated every exchange seriously. Elrond still lost, again and again, but the losses no longer felt identical. Julian could see the difference even if he did not point it out right away.

Julian kept pressing forward with the same calm force, and he did not waste time explaining every flaw. If Elrond chose too early, Julian cut around it. If Elrond tried to close a line before the attack had fully shown itself, Julian changed the line and struck through the opening Elrond had made with his own hands. The lesson moved in that way from one exchange to the next, and while Elrond kept losing, he stopped losing for the same reason each time.

Little by little, he started to read more than he had yesterday. He caught more from Julian’s shoulders, more from the way his front foot came down, more from the path the sword began to take before the strike committed. That still did not bring him victory, but it forced the exchanges to last longer.

Julian noticed.

So he pushed harder, and Elrond kept trying to read one step deeper.

By the final bout, the Academy bell was close enough that both of them could feel the lesson nearing its end. By then Elrond had already understood the mistake that kept ruining him. He had been choosing too soon. Every time he tried to answer before Julian’s attack had fully revealed itself, he gave away the exchange with his own hands. So when Julian came in again, Elrond held himself back and refused to throw out an answer at the first sign of movement.

Julian stepped in. His shoulder turned, and the wooden sword began to move.

Elrond read longer.

He did not freeze, and he did not throw out a blind guess either. He simply let Julian show a little more before he chose his answer, and because of that, his body moved later but with more purpose than before. Even so, the strike still got him in the end, and Julian still won that final exchange, but this time the loss came after a real improvement instead of another repeat of the same mistake.

Julian saw it at once.

“That’s all for today,” Julian said. “I can see you’re holding yourself back, waiting for my attack. But that might not work against someone faster than me. You need to come up with something else, Elrond.”

Elrond lowered his sword while Julian’s words settled over the result of that last exchange. The point made sense because he had already felt the weakness in what he had just done. Waiting longer had helped him, but that answer still depended too much on feel, and feel alone would not carry him against someone who moved even faster than Julian.

“Understood. That makes sense,” Elrond replied. “I can’t rely on intuition alone.”

Julian gave no long lecture after that, and that itself told Elrond enough.

From the way Julian taught, Elrond could tell something clearly. Julian was not the kind of teacher who laid every answer out in neat order and told his disciple to memorize it. He forced the problem into the clash itself, then let the flaw appear under pressure, and only after that did he point to the part that still fell short. He guided, but he did not carry. He pushed his disciple to build fighting sense with his own hands instead of handing over fixed techniques and ready-made answers.

“Speaking of which,” Julian said, “what did you discuss yesterday at the Alfrost mansion?”

He asked it only after the lesson was over, so Elrond understood then that Julian had chosen to keep training and private matters separate until now.

“Ah... it was actually... a job offer,” Elrond answered.

Even while saying it, he could hear how awkward the words sounded. He still did not have a clean way to explain what Gilbert had placed in front of him.

“A job offer?” Julian repeated.

“Yes. Lord Gilbert said he wanted to thank me, so he offered me what he called an honorable position,” Elrond said. “A guardian, sort of. He said I need to make sure the household is safe from threats. Something like that. But he doesn’t want me to think of it as being just a guard. He said I’ll have a position in the Alfrost family.”

The explanation sounded vague even to Elrond himself, and that only made the truth clearer. He still did not fully understand what the job really meant. He understood the outline of it, but not yet its full weight, and what stayed strongest in his mind was not the title itself but the fact that his life might soon be tied to House Alfrost.

“Hm... that is a vague role, to be honest,” Julian said. “But I think I understand what Gilbert is thinking.”

He paused for a moment, then spoke in the plainest way possible.

“He just wants to keep you within his reach.”

Elrond looked at him.

“Within his reach? What do you mean by that?”

“I think he sees value in you, and he doesn’t want another party to take you,” Julian said. “So he decided to snag you first. That’s my assumption. Gilbert is an opportunist, after all.”

Elrond listened without cutting in because Julian’s reading did make sense.

Julian knew Gilbert well. He was Gilbert’s senior, and in some ways an indirect mentor too, so this was not the kind of judgment he made carelessly. He had seen Gilbert notice worth before other people did, and he had seen him move on that judgment early. In the past, Julian had watched Gilbert back a merchant others overlooked, and the result later proved that Gilbert’s eye had not been wrong. To Julian, Gilbert was the kind of man who acted before others even realized there was something worth taking seriously.

“I see...” Elrond said. After that, he stayed quiet for a short while before adding, “But I still appreciate it. It will change my future too.”

“Regardless, that’s how it should be,” Julian said. “That’s also why I took you as my disciple. Your value is higher than you think, so don’t put yourself down.”

Those words stayed with Elrond because praise from Julian was never cheap. Gilbert had acted on that value, and Julian had done the same, while Elrond himself still had not learned how to measure his own worth with the same certainty.

“Understood. Thank you, Sir Julian,” Elrond replied.

Right after that, the Academy bell rang.

Julian set his wooden sword aside. Elrond put his away as well. Then the two of them packed up and left the training room.

Elrond returned to the dorm with one clear task in mind. He was leaving this place today, so there was no reason to drag it out any longer.

He opened the wardrobe and took his clothes down piece by piece, folding each one before placing it into his luggage. The dirty ones did not go into the basket this time. He gathered them with the rest, separated them properly, and packed them away so nothing would be left for the staff to deal with after he was gone.

After that, he checked the room from one end to the other. The drawers, the desk, the shelf, the bathroom, the corners near the bed, all of it passed under his eyes until he was sure he had missed nothing.

Once everything was in order, he took his bag in one hand and his new luggage in the other. He locked the door, looked at it once to make sure the latch had caught, then headed down with the key and the papers needed to return the room.

The reception desk sat where it always had in the bright entrance hall, calm and neat, as if nothing here ever changed. Elrond walked up, handed over the key and the required documents, then waited while the receptionist checked them one by one.

“That will be all, Sir Astrea,” the receptionist said as she placed the papers aside. “Your room return has been recorded.”

“Thank you for everything,” Elrond said with a small bow. “I was well taken care of here.”

She gave him a polite smile and returned the bow from behind the desk. There was nothing else to say after that, so Elrond turned and walked toward the exit.

At the door, he stopped for a moment and looked back at the Royal Academy dormitory one last time. The polished floors, the high ceiling, the quiet order of the place, all of it had already become familiar in a short span of time, and that alone said enough about how strange his life had become.

When he first stepped into Arbalest, he had only been another new student from the frontier. Now he was leaving the dorm behind to live under the roof of one of the kingdom’s highest noble houses.

The walk to Alfrost Mansion did little to settle that thought. By the time he reached the estate, the white walls and broad front path stood before him with the same polished grandeur they had shown the last time, but this time he was not here as a guest passing through.

The guard at the front gate recognized him at once and straightened. “Welcome back, Sir Elrond,” the man said as he opened the gate. “Please go right in.”

“Thank you,” Elrond said, then entered the grounds with his luggage.

He followed the main path toward the entrance while the mansion rose larger with every step. Before he could reach the door, a butler in formal attire noticed him and moved forward with practiced calm, though his eyes stayed alert as they ran over Elrond’s face and the luggage in his hands.

“Excuse me,” the butler said as he stopped in front of him. “I do not recall seeing you here before. Are you affiliated with this mansion?”

The question was polite on the surface, but the pressure behind it was plain enough. Elrond understood it immediately. A boy with luggage standing at the front entrance was not someone a butler could ignore.

“I apologize for arriving without notice,” Elrond said as he inclined his head. “My name is Elrond von Astrea. Lord Gilbert accepted me as a new guardian under House Alfrost.”

The butler’s expression changed the moment the name and title reached him. The caution remained, but it shifted into recognition, and he lowered his head at once.

“My apologies,” the butler said. “I had been informed that a new guardian would be assigned, but I failed to recognize you right away. My name is Teron Larka. You may call me Larka.”

“Elrond von Astrea,” Elrond said as he returned the bow with the same measure of formality. “Please just call me Elrond.”

“I understand, Sir Elrond,” Larka said. “Please come with me. I will show you to your room.”

Since Elrond carried more than one bag, Larka reached for one without waiting to be asked. He took the heavier piece with the ease of someone used to housework and formal service at the same time.

“Thank you,” Elrond said as he let the butler take it.

Larka gave a short nod and led the way inside. Elrond followed him through the mansion corridors, past polished floors, framed paintings, and walls that looked as if no dust had ever dared settle on them.

As they walked, Larka spoke in the steady tone of a man who had repeated the same explanations many times before. He told Elrond where meals were served and at what hours, where to leave clothes for washing, which servants he should call if he needed anything, and which parts of the mansion required notice before entering. The rules were clear, precise, and easy enough to remember.

When they finally stopped, Larka opened a door and stepped aside. “This room has been prepared for you, Sir Elrond,” he said.

Elrond entered, then stopped after only a few steps. The room before him was not some spare chamber tucked into a quiet corner for a lower retainer. It was wide, refined, and fully furnished, with a bed large enough for comfort rather than necessity, a sitting area near the window, polished cabinets, and decorations chosen with noble taste instead of mere function.

For a moment he simply stood there with the luggage still in his hand. The S-Class dorm had already been far beyond anything he had expected when he first entered the Academy, yet this room still surpassed it without effort.

In just one month, he had gone from the frontier to the capital, from a normal student room to S-Class, and now to a chamber inside Alfrost Mansion that looked like it had been prepared for someone far above his station. The pace of it all was so absurd that his mind almost rejected it on instinct.

Larka set the bag down near the cabinet and turned back toward him. “If there is anything you require, you may call for a servant at any time,” he said. “Meals follow the house schedule, and laundry will be collected if you place it in the proper basket. If you need anything beyond that, inform me directly.”

“I understand,” Elrond said.

Larka bowed once more, then moved toward the door. “Then I will leave you to settle in, Sir Elrond.”

“Thank you, Larka,” Elrond said.

The butler left, and the door closed behind him with a soft click. The room fell quiet after that, leaving Elrond alone with his luggage, the stillness, and the weight of what had just become normal.

He set the rest of his things down near the bed, then walked toward the window. When he pulled the curtain aside, the garden outside opened before him in neat lines of trimmed green, pale stone, and still water catching the light.

After looking out for a few seconds, he went back and sat on the edge of the bed. The mattress gave under his weight with a softness that made the whole room feel even more unreal.

His eyes drifted back to the window and the garden beyond it. This place was quiet, expensive, orderly, and far removed from the kind of life he should have had by birth, and that fact stayed in front of him no matter which way he looked.

'This is really nice.' Elrond thought.

As he focused more on the garden outside, he noticed someone sitting on a bench beyond the bench around tree planter, and from this distance he could barely make out blonde hair, yet that alone was enough to hold his attention a moment longer instead of letting his gaze move on.

He got up and walked to the window that opened onto the ground-floor balcony, then pushed it open and leaned out slightly for a better look, and the girl below resembled someone he knew, especially with the long blonde hair and the glimpse of her beauty he could catch from the uneven angle, but he decided not to call out because it might be inappropriate, so he left her alone and simply watched the garden scenery instead.

Not long after, a red-haired girl approached the blonde girl and the two began talking to each other, and a moment later the redhead smiled before her eyes shifted upward, and the change in her expression came out clearly as she noticed Elrond, and that reaction made the blonde girl turn her head toward him as well while the red-haired girl pointed up at him.

They were Lisoletelle and Cestina, as expected.

Elrond raised a hand and waved with a slight smile, keeping the gesture simple while watching them from above, and then the two of them started walking toward him without hesitation as if they had already decided to come over the moment they recognized him.

“Elrond!” Liso said as she arrived in front of him, her voice bright and direct while she looked up at him without holding anything back.

“Lady Lisoletelle, Lady Cestina. Good afternoon,” Elrond said with a small smile, keeping his tone steady while returning her energy in a more restrained way.

“Good afternoon, Sir Elrond,” Cestina said, her posture neat and her voice calm as she greeted him properly.

“Why are you here, Elrond?” Liso said, her curiosity coming out openly while she kept her eyes fixed on him.

“You didn’t know, Liso?” Cestina said as she answered instead, turning slightly toward her before continuing. “Sir Elrond will be living here in this mansion,” she added, stating it clearly so there would be no misunderstanding.

“LIVING HERE???” Liso said, her voice rising at once as her surprise showed without restraint. “That’s cool!! But how??”

“Sir Gilbert asked me to work for this household,” Elrond said, keeping the explanation short and direct since there was no need to expand it further.

“Hehh… I didn’t know about that,” Liso said, the surprise still in her voice as it shifted into excitement. “That’s awesome!”

“I hope you’ll enjoy living here, Elrond,” Liso added, her tone softening slightly while still carrying that same energy.

“Thank you. I hope I will,” Elrond said, and the answer came out naturally without him needing to think too much about it.

“Let’s be good comrades, Elrond!” Liso said brightly, already treating the situation as something settled on her side.

As they talked, a blue-haired girl approached from the path behind them, and Elrond noticed her coming from a distance before the others turned, but even from that distance it was clear who she was.

It was Emilia.

Elrond noticed her coming, but she didn’t seem interested at all, and the way she carried herself did not change as she drew closer, as if the conversation happening near his window had nothing to do with her.

What’s going on? Did he do something wrong?

That uneasy feeling had been lingering since their conversation in the classroom, and no matter how he went over it again in his head, Elrond still couldn’t figure out what was actually going on.

Elrond cut that thought off before it settled. He was a guardian in this house now, which meant Emilia stood above him here whether he felt at ease with that or not, and there was no reason to keep standing there while his mind ran in circles over her distance. So when she came close enough for courtesy to require it, he straightened at the open ground-floor window and greeted her first.

“Good afternoon, Lady Emilia,” Elrond said as he gave her the respect her position required and kept his voice even.

Emilia looked up at him for a moment.

“You’re already here,” Emilia said as if she were only acknowledging what was in front of her, and the reply ended so quickly that it left no room for anything more.

Her eyes moved off him right after that. She turned to Cestina and Liso instead, as though they were the ones she had come to speak to from the start, and Elrond was only part of the scenery around them. Liso caught the shift and glanced between the two of them, while Cestina held her usual calm face and waited for Emilia to continue.

“Cestina, were you here long?” Emilia said as she faced the two girls and kept her tone level.

“Only a little while, Lady Emilia,” Cestina said as she answered her at once. “We only just came over.”

“And I still didn’t know he was staying here,” Liso said as she looked up at Elrond again, her surprise still plain on her face. “You all kept that quiet.”

Before anyone else could add to it, footsteps came from inside the room behind Elrond. A butler entered and stopped near the door with the quiet precision expected inside Alfrost Mansion, then waited until Elrond turned before speaking. The interruption landed at the exact moment the conversation had begun to strain, and no one in the garden below missed that timing.

“Sir Elrond,” the butler said as he bowed his head. “Lord Gilbert requests that you come to his room.”

Elrond accepted it with a small nod. There was no reason to keep standing there after that, especially not when Emilia had already made her distance clear and Gilbert was calling for him. So he looked down at the three girls and excused himself with the same courtesy he had used from the start.

“Please pardon me, Lady Emilia, Lady Cestina, Lady Lisoletelle,” Elrond said as he inclined his head toward them. “Lord Gilbert has called for me.”

### Chapter 28: 24 - First task

#### Scene 1

As Elrond stepped out of his room, he looked back behind him inside his room. The three girls had already left as well. The unsettled feeling between him and Emilia remained in his heart, and although he could not address it at this point in time, he understood that it would have to be dealt with eventually.

When Elrond and the butler entered Gilbert's room, he immediately noticed that there was another person sitting on the couch. The atmosphere in the room felt different from before, carrying a pressure that was hard to ignore. It gave the impression that this meeting would not be a simple one.

"Lord Caelen," the butler said as he bowed respectfully toward the man before leaving the room. Seeing that, Elrond also chose to bow because it was the proper thing to do in this situation. The presence of the man alone made it clear that he was someone important.

"Good afternoon, Lord Caelen," Elrond said with a slight bow, maintaining a respectful tone.

"At ease, kid," Caelen replied in a calm but firm voice, his sharp gaze resting on Elrond as if he was already evaluating him.

"Welcome, Elrond. It seems you've already settled in," Gilbert said with a slight smile, sounding far more relaxed than the atmosphere around them suggested.

"Yes. I didn't want to waste time," Elrond replied simply, showing that he intended to take his new position seriously.

"I see. Very good, then," Gilbert said. "As you might have noticed, this is my father, Caelen Alfrost. He wanted to meet you directly." As he said that, Gilbert gestured toward Caelen with an open hand, formally presenting him.

"Nice to meet you, Lord Caelen," Elrond said again, making sure to show proper courtesy.

"'Meet' is a bit of an understatement," Caelen said as he adjusted his gloves. He paused for a brief moment, creating a heavier silence in the room before continuing. "I want to make sure you're fit for the position you've been assigned." His tone was sharp, and his eyes carefully looked Elrond over from head to toe, as though he intended to judge everything in a single glance.

"Father, we talked about this," Gilbert said, stepping in almost immediately. "And why are you talking like that?" It was obvious Gilbert did not want Caelen to push Elrond into anything unreasonable, especially when Caelen himself was one of the strongest swordsmen in Althania and could easily make the matter far more serious than it needed to be.

"Don't ruin my moment, Gilbert," Caelen said, sounding almost offended by the interruption. "I just want to confirm it. I trust you, but I still have doubts of my own." His words carried a mix of confidence and stubbornness, making it clear that he had no intention of backing down just because Gilbert was uncomfortable with it.

"Well, I don't really mind either, Sir Gilbert, Lord Caelen," Elrond replied calmly, not showing any visible hesitation despite the pressure surrounding him.

Caelen smirked when he heard that. "See? He agrees with me. It'll be fine, Gilbert," he said before standing up from the couch and straightening his tie in a composed manner. "Then let's head to the training hall."

With that, the conversation naturally came to an end and turned into action. The three of them began walking toward the sword training area together. Elrond had already noticed before that there was a training room inside the mansion, but it quickly became apparent that they were not going there. Instead, Caelen led them outside toward a separate building on the mansion grounds, which made it clear that whatever was about to happen would not be a casual test.

As Elrond, Caelen, and Gilbert entered the training hall, Elrond immediately realized why Caelen had brought them there in the first place. It was a large and spacious area, clearly meant for real and serious sparring rather than simple casual practice, and the atmosphere around them seemed to grow heavier with every step they took toward the center. The room itself almost seemed to reflect the importance of what was about to happen, and Elrond understood deep inside that this would not be an ordinary exchange.

Once they reached the middle of the hall, they each prepared their swords in silence, and that silence itself felt meaningful. Then Elrond noticed Caelen draw a real blade without even a slight hint of hesitation, which instantly made it clear that this was not going to be a harmless test or a symbolic gesture. Because of that, Elrond had no choice but to do the same, so he drew the sword he had been carrying the whole time, while Gilbert calmly stepped to the side and took the position of referee as though he had already expected this exact development from the very beginning.

Caelen then positioned himself and took a sharp stance that gave off the overwhelming impression of a veteran warrior who had walked through countless battles. In the very next moment, he cast 10x strength and 8x agility with a level of smoothness and efficiency that showed just how experienced and terrifying he truly was. Elrond’s eyes sharpened at that sight, and he responded without delay by casting 6x strength and 6x agility, which was the highest level he could currently maintain while still keeping control over himself and his body.

Gilbert stood between them for a brief moment, raised his hand into the air, and then brought it down. The instant that happened, the bout began. Both Elrond and Caelen charged toward one another at once, their movements fast and decisive, and Elrond understood right away that he could not possibly defeat Caelen through raw strength alone. Because of that, he chose the smarter route, just as he had done before when facing Julian, deciding that he would need to dodge, redirect, observe, and survive under pressure long enough to understand the flow of Caelen’s attacks.

However, Caelen’s 8x agility made that plan much more difficult than Elrond would have preferred. Caelen moved with frightening speed, and every attack carried not only force but also experience, which created a level of pressure that was hard to deal with directly. Even so, Elrond knew very well that multipliers alone did not tell the entire story, because the actual performance of enhancement magic depended on the person using it, their body, and the way they controlled mana, so he decided to challenge that overwhelming force head-on and see what he could learn from it.

A slash came down from above, clean, heavy, and fast enough to feel almost impossible to answer. Elrond barely managed to dodge and block it in time, yet he recovered quickly enough to avoid losing control of the exchange. Caelen kept pressing him with overwhelming strength and speed, forcing Elrond into defense after defense, but Elrond remained calm throughout all of it, showing no visible sign of panic even when he was pushed into narrow escapes and barely managed to dodge or block in time.

That was intentional, because Elrond understood that even if Caelen had the advantage, patterns still existed. Caelen drove in with a heavy thrust, and Elrond blocked it perfectly before sliding back and stabilizing himself, and in that instant a trace of confidence rose inside him. He stepped in and thrust from the left, Caelen deflected it, and Elrond immediately used that deflection itself as momentum for a second strike that managed to catch Caelen slightly off guard, even though Caelen still blocked it with ease and counterattacked without delay.

But Elrond had already expected that counterattack, because he had begun to read Caelen’s rhythm. He moved before the counter fully formed, shifted to Caelen’s right side, and stabbed in, forcing Caelen to pull back in time. As Caelen retreated, Elrond heard the murmur of a chant, and even though he did not immediately understand what kind of magic was being used, he charged forward anyway because the flow of the fight had already pulled him in too deeply to stop and think.

Their swords clashed once again, and by then Elrond had already grown somewhat used to Caelen’s attacks, enough to start reading their timing, pressure, and direction with greater accuracy. Then Caelen lured him into another thrust, and at the final moment he pulled back once more, revealing the true danger as a massive ice boulder suddenly formed in midair above them. Elrond saw it at once, but by then it was already too late to dodge properly, because his stance no longer carried the momentum needed to escape cleanly.

So he acted on instinct. He heated his sword with chantless magic, with no visible fire and only the heat contained inside the blade itself, and then he slashed upward with everything timed into that single motion. The ice boulder split cleanly in half, and the sight of it was so striking that even Caelen and Gilbert were momentarily caught by it as the two halves fell and shattered across the floor.

Elrond immediately returned his gaze to Caelen, ready for the next exchange and fully prepared to continue the fight. But Caelen had already lowered his sword and rested it against the floor, making it clear that the bout was over. Relief spread through Elrond at that moment, because if the battle had continued any further, there was a real chance it would have revealed far more than he wanted to show.

"That’s enough," Caelen said as he lowered his sword and looked at Elrond with the same calm face he had kept through the entire bout. He let a short pause sit between them, as if he needed that moment to settle what he had seen with his own eyes before he put it into words. "I understand now."

That was all Caelen said after the bout, and he offered nothing else before he turned and walked out of the training hall. Elrond stood where he was and watched his back disappear, still holding his sword because he could not make sense of what had just happened. He had expected more, either a sharper test or a clear judgment, so the abrupt end left him with the uncomfortable thought that he had made some mistake he had not even noticed.

"Good for you, Elrond," Gilbert said as he walked over and stopped close enough for his voice to carry without echoing through the hall. He looked toward the door Caelen had used, then back at Elrond with a small smile that carried more certainty than amusement. "Father never stops a fight until he’s already beaten his opponent. Seeing him stop in the middle like that is probably a good thing for you."

"What if I actually messed up?" Elrond said as he looked at Gilbert, and for once the worry showed on his face before he could smooth it away. The way Caelen had ended things still sat wrong in his chest because it was too brief and too clean to read. "What if I’m weaker than he imagined?"

"There’s no way," Gilbert said as he shook his head without even thinking it over. His answer came out too fast to be polite and too certain to be empty comfort, which told Elrond he meant every word. "I know Father very well. When he gets serious, he never pretends. He beats every opponent he faces, so don’t worry, Elrond. You’re approved."

With that said, the two of them left the training hall and headed back toward the mansion while the last of the cold fragments still lay scattered across the floor behind them. Gilbert walked beside Elrond through the grounds and into the main building, then stayed with him long enough to guide him toward his room even though Elrond already knew the route. The walk back was quiet, but it was the settled kind of quiet that came after something had already been decided.

"For now, you should rest," Gilbert said when they reached the corridor near Elrond’s room. He stopped there and turned slightly toward him, his tone shifting from referee and older noble to host again. "You already did the tour with Varrick, so you should be familiar with the place already. We’ll talk about your duties another day. I’m still thinking about it."

Elrond caught the implication in that and let out a faint smirk before he could stop himself. It made sense when he thought about it from Gilbert’s side because Gilbert probably had not expected him to settle into the mansion this quickly either. Between the move, the awkward meeting with Emilia, and the fight with Caelen, the day had already gone further than most people would have planned.

"Then see you later, Elrond. Enjoy your stay here," Gilbert said as he lifted a hand in a light wave before turning away.

Elrond entered his room, shut the door behind him, and dropped onto the bed with the weight of the day still clinging to his muscles. His thoughts did not stay on the fight for long because once he had a quiet place to think, his mind shifted toward what he should do next inside this mansion. That was when he remembered the barrier magic book he had learned from Selene, and because he could recall every page of it line by line, he began searching through his memory for a smaller barrier that could be adapted for use here since he had sensed no barrier protecting the mansion at all when he first arrived.

He got up, pulled out paper and a graphite pencil, and began drafting a barrier spell instead of keeping the work in his head. Most barrier magic required a catalyst, which was usually a mana stone that could hold a large amount of mana, and that was the reason barriers needed maintenance in the first place. Mana stones absorbed mana from their surroundings, and once a caster used a barrier spell with the stone as the catalyst, the stone fed mana into the circle the same way a battery in his previous world fed stored power into a machine.

That also explained the weakness built into the system. Mana stones could hold mana, but they could not hold information, so once the stored mana ran out, the barrier collapsed and disappeared with it. That was why researchers like Selene spent so much time studying mana stones in the first place, measuring how fast they absorbed mana and estimating how much a given barrier would consume so the whole structure could remain balanced instead of burning itself out.

Elrond had no catalyst on hand and no magic crystal he could borrow for the experiment, so he decided to use his own mana supply as the catalyst instead. That would make the barrier his own variation rather than a direct copy of what Selene had taught him, and that part alone kept his attention fixed on the page. He usually handled this kind of work in his head because most formulas were simple enough once he understood the logic behind them, but barrier magic carried too many linked parts to trust to memory alone when one mistake could ruin the whole spell.

Most of the formula already existed in the book he remembered, so the structure itself was not the problem. The stability of the barrier, the pace of mana consumption, and the steady output were already solved, which meant all he really had to do was replace the catalyst from a mana stone to himself and correct the flow so the spell recognized that change from beginning to end. Since his mana pool had been built through repeated training and constant control work, he knew he could function as a long-running catalyst better than most people his age ever could.

"Changing the catalyst is done. Now let’s try it," Elrond said as he set the pencil down and looked over the page one last time.

He gathered mana into his hand and began casting with the ancient language he always used when he wanted the structure of a spell to obey him without drift. The words came out clean because by now they sat in his mind as firmly as numbers in an old formula.

*"Will of the spirit that flows through my veins, wake from my flesh and bone and surge as an unyielding tide of protection, gather and weave into a radiating mana lattice of absolute iron, expanding to lock the space around me into a sanctuary of stillness, take form as the eternal aegis that does not break, and become the unyielding wall that stands between my life and the dark until the final spark is spent."*

Light bloomed the moment the spell took shape, and Elrond’s eyes narrowed at once because it came out far brighter than it should have. He had only built a small barrier and had fed it a limited amount of mana, yet the glow still flared hard enough to ruin the whole point of using it indoors without attracting attention. He stared at the spell for another moment, felt how much mana it was drawing, and clicked his tongue in irritation.

"This isn’t right," Elrond said as he watched the light hold around him. He lifted one hand and felt the barrier’s pull on his mana more carefully, checking the response instead of dismissing it as a failed draft. "It draws too much mana, and it’s too bright. What went wrong here?"

He returned to the paper and started reformulating the chant, changing one line, then another, then the flow between them, and each new attempt forced him to compare the language against the structure in his head. Minutes stretched into hours while page after page filled with notes, crossed-out phrases, and quick corrections written wherever he found space. He tested multiple variations and refined both the wording and the mana flow until the first version no longer looked like a finished spell at all and instead looked like what it really was, which was a rough draft that had failed its first real use.

Eventually he found a version that sat right with him. The logic held, the mana path read cleaner, and the phrasing no longer wasted power on visible output that served no purpose. He straightened, drew in another controlled breath, and spoke again in the ancient tongue.

*"Spirit that slumbers within the temple of bone, wake and flow as the deep river that knows no storm, let the current of my life rest in the stillness of the mirror, untouched by the shadows that would hollow the marrow. Weave the threads of the soul into a lattice of absolute silence, locking the breath of the world into an unyielding sanctuary of iron, take form as the eternal aegis that does not shatter, and become the invisible wall between the living light and the coming dark until the final spark returns to the stars."*

A soft light wrapped around his body this time instead of bursting out across the room. It held for a moment, then faded from sight, and when Elrond reached out with his senses, the barrier was still there exactly as he wanted it, present but hidden from the human eye. A smile pulled at his mouth before he even thought about it because the result matched the picture he had been working toward from the start.

"Finally," Elrond said as he let out the word and then dispersed the barrier himself.

He pushed back from the desk and only then noticed the state of the room around him. Papers had spread across the tabletop and slipped onto the floor while he worked, some covered in full lines of formula and others marked with half-finished corrections where he had abandoned one approach for another. He bent down, gathered them into a stack, and set them aside to throw away later once he decided which versions were worth keeping for reference.

Then he noticed the time. The light outside had already shifted, and the mansion had fallen into the quieter rhythm that came before the evening meal. It was close to dinner already, so Elrond left his room and headed toward the center of the mansion.

While walking toward the center of the mansion, Elrond passed by a few maids and butlers who were still moving around and carrying out their duties. The mansion had grown quieter than before, yet there was still enough activity around him to remind him that this was a place filled with many people who all had their own roles to play. Not long after that, he happened to run into Varrick, who looked as though he had been heading somewhere with a specific purpose in mind.

"Good evening, Sir Elrond," Varrick said politely as he came to a stop in front of him. His manner remained respectful and professional, and it was obvious from the timing that he had been looking for Elrond rather than meeting him there by chance. "I was about to go to your room. Dinner is ready. Would you like to eat in the dining room?"

"Good evening, Varrick," Elrond replied, returning the greeting without any issue. At first he was about to refuse because he had something else on his mind, but then he paused and thought about the situation more carefully, since he still was not fully used to how things worked in the mansion yet. "No, no... I just wanted to do something. Should I eat in the dining room?"

"No need to worry, Sir Elrond," Varrick said, answering in a calm and reassuring way that made the situation easier to understand. He seemed to already know exactly what information Elrond needed to hear. "Currently, no one is in the dining room. It seems Lord Gilbert, Lady Emilia, and Lord Caelen are all busy, so they decided to eat in their own rooms. If you want, I can bring your meal to your room right away."

"I see. They’re very busy indeed," Elrond said after hearing that explanation, accepting the situation without any complaint because it made sense considering everything that had happened during the day. The mansion really did seem to be full of people with responsibilities that could not simply be ignored. "Understood, then. I’ll do the same. Can you place it on the table inside? I need to take care of something first."

"Understood. I will prepare it right away. Please excuse me," Varrick said, then bowed and left so he could make the necessary arrangements for Elrond’s dinner.

After that, Elrond continued walking toward the middle of the mansion, but he did not stop there. Instead, he stepped outside and made his way up to the roof, because that was the place that made the most sense for what he intended to do next. Once he had settled himself there, he opened his hand in front of him with the palm facing upward and closed his eyes, allowing his attention to narrow entirely toward the spell he meant to cast.

He then began chanting the final version of the spell he had written down and memorized earlier. As the words left his mouth, mana started to gather above his palm, and the light that formed there became tighter and denser with each passing moment, swirling inward as though it were being compressed into a point that was close to bursting apart. Elrond remained focused throughout the process, because he understood that the smallest mistake at this stage could ruin the entire purpose of what he was trying to accomplish.

When Elrond finally finished the chant, the gathered light spread outward in a spherical wave that expanded from him and moved across the mansion grounds. The effect resembled an early scanner, because it began detecting anything that was already within the mansion and the surrounding area. Anyone it recognized as already being inside was marked as safe, which meant they would be able to pass through without resistance later, and while some people noticed the wave of light as it moved outward, others failed to notice it at all because it happened so quickly.

Elrond stayed where he was and maintained his concentration the entire time, making sure the spell fully covered the mansion instead of leaving behind any unseen gaps. He followed the reach of the expanding wave with careful attention until it stretched all the way to the edge of the grounds. Once it reached that point, he stopped feeding mana into it, and although the visible light faded away soon after, the barrier itself remained in place as intended.

At that point, Elrond could already sense the spell responding to his will. The barrier would now alert him to dangerous intent, or to an unknown presence that had not been detected and accepted when the barrier first spread throughout the mansion. The result was exactly the kind of effect he had wanted, and it gave him a practical layer of awareness that had not existed around the mansion before.

"Nice. Everyone currently in the mansion is detected," Elrond muttered to himself as he considered the result with quiet satisfaction. He was already thinking past the first success and toward the next part that still needed to be solved. "Now I need to make sure anyone new entering is actually safe."

Once he had confirmed that the barrier was functioning as intended, Elrond dropped down from the roof instead of climbing back down the way he had come. The moment he landed, two guards nearby noticed him and immediately snapped into defensive stances, reacting with the kind of speed that showed they took their duty seriously. Their suspicion was natural, because from their point of view, someone had just appeared from above without warning.

"Who is that?" one of the guards demanded in a sharp voice as he prepared himself for a possible threat.

"Ah... sorry to startle you. I’m Elrond," Elrond replied, giving his answer without making any sudden movement that might worsen the misunderstanding.

"Oh, Sir Elrond," one of the guards said after recognizing him properly, and the tension in his posture eased once he understood who he was dealing with. Elrond’s name had apparently spread through the mansion faster than he had expected, because even guards he had never spoken to seemed to know about him already. "What were you doing up there?"

"Uhm... I was setting up a barrier," Elrond answered, choosing the simple truth because there was little point in inventing something else. "Wait, you know me?" Elrond curious how they already know him.

"Of course you were," the first guard said, his tone carrying a mixture of disbelief and rough humor that showed what he really thought of the situation. The idea of a newcomer appearing, being assigned as guardian, and then casually standing on the roof to cast barrier magic clearly struck him as something unusual even for a noble house. "A new guy suddenly appears and gets assigned as guardian. It’s rare."

Before the conversation could become any more awkward than that, the other guard quickly elbowed his companion in the side. The warning was immediate and effective, and it made it clear that even if the thought itself was understandable, it was not the sort of thing that should be said aloud to Elrond’s face. The second guard then stepped forward slightly so he could smooth things over before the moment grew worse.

"I apologize for my friend’s rudeness, Sir Elrond," the second guard said, lowering his head respectfully.

"No worries. It’s fine," Elrond replied, deciding not to take offense because he understood why the man had reacted that way in the first place.

"I see. Thank you, then," the guard said, relieved that Elrond had not chosen to make an issue out of it. His tone settled back into proper formality, and the matter ended there without any further trouble. "Please excuse us, Sir Elrond. Good evening."

After the two guards moved on, Elrond went back inside the mansion. By then the building had become much quieter than it had been earlier, and the sense of activity that usually filled the halls had dropped away into something calmer and more subdued. He returned straight to his room, closed the window he had left open before going outside, and then lay down on his bed to call it a day.

---

On the other side of the mansion, after the bout between Caelen and Elrond had already come to an end, Caelen went back to Gilbert’s room and waited there by himself. He sat there in silence for some time, clearly thinking about what had just happened in the training hall and what kind of person Elrond truly was. After a while, Gilbert finally returned to the room as well.

"Took you long enough," Caelen said when he saw Gilbert come in.

"I walked Elrond to his room," Gilbert replied, explaining the reason for his delay. Then he paused for a brief moment, because the question he wanted to ask had already been in his head from the start. "How is he?" Gilbert asked.

"To put it simply," Caelen said, pausing once again as if he was choosing the right words, "he’s a beast."

Gilbert froze for a moment after hearing that answer. He genuinely could not remember his father ever describing anyone like that before, which made those words feel heavier than usual. Because of that, Gilbert immediately realized that Caelen’s evaluation of Elrond was far beyond ordinary praise.

"What do you mean by that, Father?" Gilbert asked genuinely, because he wanted to understand exactly what Caelen had seen during the fight.

"How much enhancement do you think I used during that bout?" Caelen asked instead of answering directly, clearly wanting Gilbert to think about the situation more carefully.

"I wasn’t paying attention to your magic in detail," Gilbert admitted honestly. He thought back to the fight and tried to estimate it based on what he had seen from the side. "But I’d guess five times or six times?"

"That’s wrong," Caelen replied calmly, without changing his expression at all. "I intentionally used ten times strength and eight times agility from the start." Caelen had clearly been using the fight to test Elrond’s situational awareness from the very beginning, not merely to pressure him for appearances.

"No way. You pushed that to the limit?" Gilbert said, visibly surprised by that answer, because even he understood how much pressure that level of enhancement would create in an actual exchange.

"Yes," Caelen answered. "In that moment, there were only two possibilities. Either he trembles in fear, or he stays quiet because he has no clue." Caelen paused again before continuing, his eyes narrowing slightly as he recalled the beginning of the fight. "But Elrond didn’t flinch. So I thought he had no clue."

Gilbert stayed quiet and listened, knowing there had to be more to it than that. He understood his father well enough to know that Caelen would never stop a real test in the middle just because someone stayed calm for a short while. That meant something in Elrond’s actions had changed Caelen’s judgment during the bout itself.

"I was ready to beat him down," Caelen continued, speaking with complete honesty and without softening his words. "But he charged at me head-on, even with lower enhancement. And the way he fought... he understood the situation. He controlled himself and fought smarter. Even against that strength gap, he managed my attacks. And near the end, he started reading the pattern of my swordplay."

Gilbert let out a slow breath after hearing that explanation. What Caelen described matched what Julian had already reported before, though hearing the same conclusion from his father made it feel even more real. It also made Gilbert realize once again that Elrond’s talent was far beyond what most people would ever expect from someone his age.

"Just like what Julian explained," Gilbert said, recalling Julian’s earlier report in his mind.

"Yes. I wanted to confirm it myself," Caelen replied. His voice stayed calm and measured, but by now it was obvious that he had already reached a firm conclusion about Elrond. "If the fight continued, I probably would’ve lost. I’m old, and I don’t have the energy to keep improvising."

Gilbert looked at his father in silence for a moment after hearing those words. That kind of admission was not something Caelen would say lightly, especially not in private and especially not about a boy who had only just entered the mansion. Because of that, the meaning behind it felt even heavier than Caelen’s earlier description.

Caelen let the silence settle for a short while, then he added one final remark.

"You did well, Gilbert, taking that kid into this household," Caelen said.

"I won’t disappoint you, Father," Gilbert replied.

---

The next day, Elrond woke up as usual and went out early in the morning to check the central training area inside the mansion. When he arrived there, he saw that it was still empty, and because of that he hesitated a little about whether it was fine for him to use it by himself. Since he was still new to the mansion and did not want to assume too much, he decided it would be better to ask first rather than simply step in and start using the place on his own.

"Excuse me, is it allowed to use the training hall in the center?" Elrond asked when he saw a guard who happened to be on patrol nearby.

"Good morning, Sir Elrond. Yes, feel free to use it," the guard replied, stopping as he answered him properly. "It’s rarely used, but usually Sir Gilbert or Lady Emilia uses that training hall."
