"I see. Thank you," Elrond said, ending the conversation there since that was all he needed to know.

After that, Elrond walked toward the entrance to the training area, which was the same place he had usually only watched from the windows in the center of the mansion before. Once he stepped outside, the whole space immediately felt open and wide around him in a way that was different from how it looked from inside. It was a semi-outdoor training hall, and a paved stone path led toward a clean rectangular practice ground in the center, while trimmed grass and neatly planted trees surrounded it, and there were also some benches nearby that made it look like a place where people could relax and watch as well as train.

Elrond stopped at the edge of the practice area and let out a long breath as he looked at the place in front of him. Winter was going to arrive in a few more weeks, and the morning cold had already become sharp enough that mist came out from his mouth each time he breathed. Even so, he did not waste much time just standing there, because once he had taken in the atmosphere of the place, he immediately began his usual workout.

He started with push-ups, sit-ups, and the rest of the physical exercises he always did before picking up his sword. He kept going until his body finally warmed up properly and the cold no longer bothered him the same way it had at first. Once that was done, he picked up the sword he had set down earlier, adjusted his stance carefully, and began replaying every bout he had fought in his mind, whether it was against his father, Julian, or Caelen, because every one of those fights was still perfectly clear in his memory.

Then he started to swing.

From the outside, it might have looked strange, almost like he was sparring against empty air for no reason at all, because there was no opponent standing in front of him. But inside Elrond’s mind, everything was clear and vivid, and the movements he made were not random in the slightest. He was following opponents that he could still see through memory, strike by strike, step by step, and because of that every swing had its own purpose.

Inside the mansion, workers continued passing through the hallways and carrying out their duties, and now and then some of them happened to glance out through the windows and notice Elrond practicing outside by himself. Most of them only looked briefly before moving on again, but one of the people who passed by was Emilia. When she noticed that it was Elrond out there training alone, she stopped by the window and watched him.

As Emilia stood there observing him, Gilbert happened to pass by as well and noticed that she had stopped.

"What are you doing?" Gilbert asked when he saw her standing by the window instead of continuing on her way.

"Nothing," Emilia replied, though she did not look away from the training ground outside. "I was just watching an unusual scene."

"Ah... is that Elrond?" Gilbert said, following her line of sight until he noticed the figure outside.

"I think so," Emilia answered.

"No wonder he’s so talented," Gilbert said after watching for a short while and seeing how focused Elrond was even at this hour. "He’s already training this early in the morning."

"I see," Emilia said coldly, giving the answer in a tone that made it sound as though she did not care about it at all. "Well, it’s not my business."

But what she said and what she actually felt were not the same thing. As Emilia watched Elrond practice by himself in the cold morning like that, it became even clearer to her why he had become so strong in the first place, and that thought left an uncomfortable feeling inside her. There was jealousy there, but there was also awe, and because both feelings were mixed together in a way she could not properly sort out, she could not express them clearly even to herself.

Gilbert noticed enough to understand that something was still awkward between Emilia and Elrond, but he hesitated to pry into it. He felt that forcing the issue right now would only make things worse, so he chose to simply observe for the moment and let it be as it was. Even so, while watching Elrond, he had already started thinking about what kind of first assignment Elrond could be given as the guardian of this household.

"Heh..." Gilbert smirked, and after that he paused for a moment and closed his eyes briefly as though some idea had just come to him.

"What is that look?" Emilia asked when she noticed the expression on his face, because she knew very well that Gilbert never made that kind of face for no reason.

"Nothing," Gilbert said, though it was obvious from the way he answered that it was not really nothing at all. Then he looked back toward the training ground again and made his decision. "Well, I should join him. It’s been too long since I swung my sword."

With that, Gilbert started walking away, leaving Emilia behind by the window.

Emilia stared at his back for a moment, then frowned slightly as she remembered something. By the time he was already near the exit door, she raised her voice so he could still hear her.

"Weren’t you hunting the Dire Wolf two days ago?!" Emilia called out.

Gilbert did not answer her at all. He simply kept walking as though he had not heard anything, passed through the exit, and headed toward the training ground outside. Through the window, Emilia watched him approach Elrond and greet him there, and that was the last thing she saw before she finally turned away and moved on to her other tasks.

"Yo, Elrond. You started training already?" Gilbert said as he approached the training ground with an easy and relaxed expression on his face, looking at Elrond as though he had stumbled onto an interesting sight first thing in the morning.

"Oh... Sir Gilbert. Good morning," Elrond replied politely as he turned toward him after hearing his voice. Even though he had already been told that he was allowed to use the training hall, he still felt a little uneasy about making use of a place inside the mansion so freely when he had only just arrived recently. "Sorry for using the training hall without asking permission."

"What are you talking about?" Gilbert said in a casual tone, sounding almost surprised that Elrond would even think such a thing in the first place. To Gilbert, the matter was simple, and there was no reason for Elrond to be so stiff about it. "You’re free to use anything in this mansion." He paused for a moment after saying that, then smiled a little before continuing. "Do you mind if I join? Don’t worry, I’m not like my father. This is just pure training."

"S-Sure... we can try," Elrond said after a brief pause, agreeing even though he still felt slightly caught off guard by how casually Gilbert had stepped into the situation. Even so, he had no real reason to refuse, and there was also a part of him that was curious about how Gilbert would fight compared to Caelen. Because of that, he accepted without saying anything more than necessary.

Elrond then bent down and carefully set his sword aside before moving into position. Gilbert also gave him enough space, and the two of them naturally separated until there was a proper distance between them for a practice bout. After that, each of them picked up a wooden sword, making it clear that this would be a real spar but without the level of danger that had been present when Caelen tested him.

"Please go easy on me, Sir Gilbert," Elrond said as he adjusted his grip and looked at Gilbert with a calm but focused expression.

"I should be the one saying that," Gilbert replied, sounding amused as he raised his wooden sword and settled into his own stance.

The two of them faced each other in silence after that, each taking their stance properly and preparing themselves for the exchange. The air between them seemed to tighten as both of them readied themselves, because even if Gilbert called it pure training, neither of them looked like they intended to hold back much once the bout started. They stood there with their wooden swords in hand, ready to go all out for the bout.

### Chapter 29: 25 - Alignment

#### Scene 1

Elrond did not know what Gilbert was about to show him. Gilbert took a stance that looked very similar to Caelen’s, and the resemblance pulled Elrond’s focus tighter. Once they were set, they began the bout.

Gilbert came forward with attacks that felt light at first, yet each one carried a strange sharpness. Most of his swings answered whatever Elrond did first, as though he waited for the move and stepped into it with exact timing. That did not come from talent alone. Elrond quickly picked up on the pattern in Gilbert’s fighting and felt that something was off.

Gilbert was a thinker and an opportunist. He found openings where other people saw nothing and turned them to his advantage. When he observed Elrond, he did not see only a talented boy. He saw someone who could become valuable to House Alfrost, and to his own position within it.

Gilbert wanted to test whether Elrond could actually see through him or accept his movements as ordinary skill. He activated Converging Possibilities, an ability within Sovereign Prescience that allowed him to perceive future paths.

Converging Possibilities let Gilbert see up to ten seconds into the future. What appeared before him was a flickering set of ghostlike outcomes, translucent outlines of actions and results shaped by the timing and movement already present in the bout. He used that advantage against Elrond to see whether Elrond could sense what was happening.

The bout soon began to feel stale. Elrond followed every strike Gilbert threw at him, and at first he assumed Gilbert was only toying with him because this was just a bout. But the longer they exchanged blows, the clearer it became that Gilbert was serious. He watched Elrond the same way Elrond watched other people in combat.

That was when Elrond noticed the mismatch.

The longer he fought, the more it felt as though Gilbert could see through his movements before they fully took shape. It was as though Gilbert already knew what Elrond would do before Elrond himself had fully committed. The feeling remained no matter how many times Elrond changed his angle or rhythm.

Elrond took some distance and paused to test Gilbert more carefully. He raised his magic perception and searched for any trace of magic on him, but found nothing. The contradiction only sharpened. If Gilbert was using some unnatural advantage, Elrond should have sensed mana moving somewhere. Divine blessings, however, worked differently. They were inborn phenomena, and Elrond still could not properly perceive them with the senses he relied on.

The answer in his mind stayed the same.

'I cannot sense any magic at all on him,' Elrond thought.

He did not want to rely on suspicion alone, so he tested it again. He engaged Gilbert once more, trading strike after strike and adjusting his movement repeatedly, until it became clear that Gilbert was predicting him. Gilbert did not only answer obvious actions. He also met Elrond’s uncertain movements before they fully settled, and that was the part Elrond could not dismiss.

So Elrond backed off again.

“Sir Gilbert, that’s unfair,” Elrond said as he lowered his wooden sword slightly, though his attention never left Gilbert. “I thought it was just a bout. Did you use something?”

Gilbert smiled and paused, as though he had been waiting for Elrond to call it out.

“Hahaha... so I got caught,” Gilbert replied, amused. He paused before continuing. “Yes, I did. But before I explain, there’s one thing I want to confirm with you, Elrond.”

“What is it?” Elrond asked, still cautious.

“Do you trust me, Elrond?” Gilbert asked, and this time his tone turned serious. Revealing a divine blessing meant revealing a true secret.

“What do you mean by that, Sir Gilbert? Of course I trust you,” Elrond replied at first, because the answer seemed obvious.

“It’s not that simple,” Gilbert said. “What I mean is, do you fully trust me?”

Elrond paused after hearing that, because now he understood Gilbert was asking for something much heavier than ordinary trust. Fully trusting him meant trusting every decision Gilbert made about Elrond’s place in this household. It meant tying himself even deeper to House Alfrost than he already had.

When Elrond thought about it, he realized he had already taken that step the moment he accepted Gilbert’s offer and entered this mansion. He closed his eyes, considered the question, and made his decision.

“If you mean every action you take, then I fully trust you, Sir Gilbert,” Elrond said seriously when he opened his eyes again. “I already tied my life within the Alfrost household, which means you are the line I fully trust.”

“That’s what I wanted to hear,” Gilbert replied. He paused again, and relief showed on his face. “Because I fully trust you, Elrond. You have a future I intend to protect, and I will make sure that happens.”

Elrond looked surprised by that answer. Gilbert was placing real expectation on him. That landed on Elrond more heavily than he had expected.

“I-I’m honored,” Elrond said, hesitating because he had not been ready for words like that.

“Then let me tell you one of my biggest secrets,” Gilbert said, pausing before he spoke again. “I have a divine blessing to see the future.”

The moment Elrond heard that, everything clicked into place.

“That explains the bout earlier,” Elrond said, trying to sound casual.

“Well, seeing the future is a bit much,” Gilbert replied, correcting the phrasing. “The future is made of possibilities. What I see are those possibilities. The closer I get to an event, the clearer it becomes. I activated that ability on purpose to see whether you could see through it, and you did.”

“That’s a useful ability,” Elrond said. He narrowed his eyes. “And dangerous, I’d say.”

“You don’t seem that surprised,” Gilbert said as he watched Elrond’s face with interest. “But you’re right. It’s useful and it’s dangerous. That’s why I kept it secret. That means you are the fifth person who knows.”

“I’ve met a bunch of divine blessing users already,” Elrond said with a smile. “It just happens that I’m surrounded by people who have them, so it doesn’t surprise me anymore.”

As he said that, Elrond began counting in his head and trying to guess who the other four might be. His mind moved quickly from one possible name to another, Emilia, Caelen, Gilbert’s late mother, Cestina, and himself.

“It was my father, Emilia, Cestina, and Julian,” Gilbert said, catching Elrond’s thinking almost immediately.

“Oh, I see,” Elrond replied. “So it was Julian. I thought it was your late mother.”

Gilbert shook his head. “My mother passed away before this blessing revealed.”

Silence settled between them for a moment. Gilbert had chosen to reveal one of his deepest secrets, and Elrond understood that the trust Gilbert had spoken about was real. Elrond’s answer had been real as well, so neither of them needed to say anything more.

After the bout, Gilbert sheathed the wooden sword and looked at Elrond. Elrond put away his own sword and waited for him to speak.

"Anyway, I've been trying to think about what you can do," Gilbert said as he crossed his arms.

"Oh, actually... about that," Elrond replied. "Last night, I put a barrier on the mansion."

"Oh... that sounds good, but I want to..." Gilbert started, then stopped.

A barrier over an entire noble mansion was not something a person casually put up overnight.

"You what?!" Gilbert blurted out.

"Eh?" Elrond said. "I put a barrier on the mansion. Sorry for not telling you beforehand. Did I mess up?"

"No, no. You didn't do anything wrong," Gilbert said, waving a hand once. "But that is very hard to do, isn't it? It requires a mana crystal, a lot of mana to supply it, and proper planning."

"Ah... yes, that's right," Elrond said. He understood he could not say he had figured everything out in one night, so he chose his words. "My mother taught me, and I've seen barriers used many times while living here, so I figured out how to do it."

It was not entirely false. He had learned from his mother, but what he had done last night went far beyond simple observation.

"I see," Gilbert said. "So you're used to it. But that doesn't explain the catalyst. Did you put a mana crystal somewhere?"

"About that... I didn't use any mana crystal," Elrond admitted honestly. "It's too expensive for me to purchase."

"What? Then what did you use to supply the barrier?" Gilbert asked.

"I used my own mana reserve to supply it," Elrond said, as if it were nothing unusual.

"I see, you used your own mana..." Gilbert said, then pinched the bridge of his nose and let out a breath halfway between disbelief and exhaustion.

"I don't understand you, Elrond," Gilbert said. "How many times have you surprised me already? But never like this. How are you able to supply a barrier like that? From what I know, barriers require mana crystals because they need a stable supply."

"Oh, that's not a problem," Elrond replied. "It's a small barrier, and it alerts me to bad intentions and unknown people passing through. The mana supply isn't that much. As long as I can replenish it, I'll be fine."

"But isn't that exhausting?" Gilbert asked.

"Not at all," Elrond said. "Ah... I think I should share my secret with you, Sir Gilbert. I have an extremely high mana pool. I thought you already knew because Teach Julian gave you a report."

"I know you have a large mana pool," Gilbert said, "but I never thought it was enough to sustain a barrier like that."

Short-term combat barriers were one thing. Using himself as a long-term source for one like this was something else entirely.

"You don't need to worry, Sir Gilbert," Elrond said. "Even if I stop replenishing my mana, the barrier will keep running for more than two months."

He still kept most of his mana suppressed. There was no reason to let anyone with appraisal abilities see how much he truly had.

"If you say so, then I won't argue," Gilbert said at last, sounding like he had decided to accept it for now even if he still had questions. "I'd like to hear more about that barrier later. But for now, I want to give you a task."

"What is it?" Elrond asked.

"Since you and Emilia are in the same class, I want you to protect her from any danger in the academy if something happens," Gilbert said. "Other noble houses have also been dealing with trouble, so we need to be wary anywhere. Even the academy is not guaranteed to be safe."

"I see. I can do that," Elrond replied calmly.

He still did not understand why Emilia acted that way around him, and the question had stayed with him since he entered the household. If he had to stay close to her anyway, then this might give him a chance to understand her better.

"Good," Gilbert said, satisfied with that answer.

Elrond's stomach growled loudly.

In the quiet training hall, Gilbert looked at him, amusement and disbelief meeting on his face. Elrond looked away, embarrassed now that the hunger had finally caught up to him.

"It seems you haven't eaten," Gilbert said.

"Sorry, Sir Gilbert," Elrond admitted. "I forgot to eat dinner last night after putting up the barrier and fell asleep immediately after."

"Then go eat breakfast and prepare for the academy," Gilbert said.

"Then please excuse me, Sir Gilbert," Elrond replied respectfully.

He tidied himself up and left the training hall. He returned to his room first to change clothes, thinking breakfast should come next before he left for the academy. But once he got there, he realized he did not actually know how to request breakfast in a noble mansion like this.

Just as Elrond finished changing clothes, someone knocked on the door to his room. He opened it quickly without making the person wait for too long, and when he did, he saw a butler standing there while holding a covered tray in his hands. It looked like the mansion had already prepared breakfast for him without him even needing to ask, which made him realize that he had worried for nothing.

"Sir Elrond, breakfast is ready," the butler said in a respectful tone while holding the tray carefully in front of him.

The butler stepped inside the room after that and walked over to the table without wasting any time. He placed the tray down properly, then lifted the lid and revealed what had been prepared for the morning meal. Inside were bread, some meat on the side, and a bowl of soup that still had some warmth rising from it.

"Please enjoy, Sir Elrond," the butler said before leaving the room again once everything had been set in place.

"Thank you," Elrond replied politely.

Elrond sat down and began eating the breakfast immediately because his hunger from skipping dinner last night had still not gone away. He dipped the bread into the soup and ate it like that, finding the taste simple and plain, but it was more than enough for the morning and that was what mattered right now. It was not an especially memorable meal, but it did its job well enough and filled his stomach.

After finishing breakfast, Elrond put on his academy uniform and prepared himself to leave for school. It was probably around seven in the morning by then, and the soft light coming in through the window made that feel about right. As he got ready, he thought about how this was really his first proper morning in the mansion after everything that had happened, the bout with Caelen, the barrier he had put on the mansion, and the early morning bout with Gilbert, and he assumed that this kind of routine would probably become normal for him sooner or later.

Once he had everything packed and ready, he left his room and started heading toward the mansion entrance. On the way there, he passed several butlers, maids, and guards, and all of them greeted him properly as he walked by. Elrond returned those greetings while still feeling that he had not fully gotten used to living in a place like this yet, because every little part of the mansion moved with the kind of order and polish that made the difference between this life and his old home very obvious.

Right as he reached the entrance, he saw Emilia already there wearing her academy uniform, which looked similar to his own. The sight startled him for a moment because he had not expected to run into her like that at the entrance first thing in the morning. For just a second, he stood there caught off guard before he quickly gave her a proper greeting.

"G-Good morning, Lady Emilia," Elrond said, surprised by seeing her there.

"Good morning," Emilia replied in a cool tone. She gave him only a brief glance before looking away again and closing her eyes, as though she had no intention of continuing the exchange beyond that.

Elrond paused after that, and an awkward silence settled between them almost immediately. He tried to think of something to say, but nothing good came to mind fast enough, and the air between them felt stiff in a way that made even a simple sentence seem like it could make things worse. He was just about to say something anyway when the carriage driver opened the door and greeted Emilia before he had the chance.

"Lady Emilia, the carriage is ready," the driver said in a respectful manner. Then he noticed Elrond standing there as well and spoke again. "Oh, Sir Elrond is already here. Sir Gilbert asked me to bring you as well."

That suggestion immediately felt strange to Elrond. Riding in the same carriage as Emilia already seemed uncomfortable enough because of the current atmosphere between them, and when he glanced at Emilia, he could tell that even though her face still looked calm on the surface, she clearly did not like the idea either. Because of that, Elrond decided it would be better to refuse instead of making the situation worse for her.

"Oh... sorry. I think I prefer to walk," Elrond said.

"I see. Understood, Sir Elrond," the driver replied. Then he turned back toward Emilia and addressed her again. "After you, Lady Emilia."

Emilia walked over to the carriage and boarded it without saying anything else. Elrond stayed where he was and watched her go, already certain that refusing had been the better choice. Riding in the same carriage as Emilia could easily create trouble for her, and it could also damage her reputation if other people began connecting her too closely with a commoner like him, especially in a place like the academy where noble students paid attention to things like that.

Because of that, Elrond chose to walk to the academy by himself. He already knew the route well enough, so there was no real inconvenience in doing that, and on foot it would only take around fifteen minutes anyway. So after the carriage left, Elrond set off toward the Royal Academy alone.

When Elrond arrived at the classroom, everything still looked basically the same as usual. The desks were all in their normal places, and the students were already there talking like they always did in the morning. The only real difference was that Elrond had come later than he normally did, so that naturally drew some attention.

"Yo, Elrond. You're pretty late," Leon said as he glanced at him while Elrond came over and sat down beside him.

"Oh... yeah. I had something to do this morning," Elrond replied in a casual way. Of course, he could not just openly say that he was living at the Alfrost mansion now, because that would only raise more questions than he wanted to deal with right now. So he gave Leon a vague answer instead and hoped that would be enough.

"That makes me wonder, do you live in the dorm?" Leon asked, sounding suspicious now that Elrond had answered in such an unclear way.

"Yes... kind of," Elrond said.

"Kind of?" Leon repeated, clearly not satisfied with that answer at all. "Do you live somewhere else?" he pressed, because Leon was the kind of person who would not just let something weird pass by without asking more about it.

"Uh, yeah. It depends on what I need," Elrond answered, still keeping it as vague as possible because he did not want to say too much.

"Uwoh, cool," Leon said, sounding impressed in his own way. "You do adventurer jobs too, don't you?"

"Yes. It's related to that," Elrond said. That answer was close enough to the truth that he could say it without feeling too dishonest, and it was also vague enough that Leon would probably not keep digging into it too much. At least, that was what Elrond hoped.

While they were talking like that, Elrond's attention kept drifting toward Emilia's seat every now and then. He had already been told by Gilbert to protect her if anything happened in the academy, so naturally he could not help checking on her from time to time. One of those glances lasted just a little too long, and Liso noticed it right away.

The moment their eyes met, Liso immediately reacted like usual. She lifted her hand with her bright energy and called out to him from her seat without caring how much attention she was pulling toward herself. That was just the kind of person she was, and there was no hesitation in her at all.

"Good morning, Elrond!" Liso said loudly as she waved.

Her voice was loud enough that both Cestina and Emilia looked over because of it. Cestina saw Elrond and gave him a light wave along with a small smile that felt calm and warm without making a big deal out of it. Emilia also looked at him, but her expression stayed the same as always, cold and distant, and after that brief look she turned away again like she did not want to continue that moment any longer than necessary.

"What a noisy girl, first thing to do in the morning," Leon complained the moment he heard Liso shouting across the classroom like that.

Of course, Liso heard him say that. She turned toward Leon right away, and the two of them started going back and forth with exaggerated gestures and mocking faces like they had fallen into some silly routine they both understood perfectly well.

To Elrond, the whole thing looked exactly like something pulled straight out of a shonen manga he had read in his previous life, and because of that, even with everything else going on around him, he could not help thinking how ridiculous and familiar it looked at the same time.

As someone who still retained the memories of his previous life, Elrond naturally kept comparing this world to the one he used to live in little by little. The more he lived in it and observed things carefully, the more similarities he found, to the point that it often made him feel as though this world was reflecting Earth in a strange and incomplete way. Even something as basic as time followed the same kind of structure he remembered, with days measured through sunrise and sunset before being divided into weeks, months, seasons, and years, and that alone was already enough to make Elrond doubt that this system had simply been invented here without any outside influence.

After reading more books about the world, Elrond found even more things that felt far too familiar to be dismissed as coincidence. Because of that, he slowly came to one conclusion in his mind, that someone besides him must have been reincarnated into this world at some point, someone who had also retained memories from a previous life and introduced certain ideas here long before Elrond himself ever noticed them. The only major thing that did not match at all was the map of the world, because it looked completely different from the Earth he once knew, but aside from that, so many things around him still carried the same kind of familiarity that it felt like a medieval world shaped by traces of something more modern.

Another thing that stood out to him was the way language and algebra were studied here, because both of them were extremely similar to what he had learned in his previous life. The structure of written language, the way numbers started from zero and continued upward, and even the most basic formulas for shapes like triangles and squares all matched what he already remembered. Since Elrond had once lived as a scientist, he could easily recall many theories and principles from memory, including ideas related to circles and other geometric studies, but he knew very well that revealing such knowledge too suddenly would be dangerous, so he remained cautious and kept most of those thoughts to himself while quietly spending his free time experimenting and thinking through scientific ideas on his own.

Even astronomy gave him that same familiar feeling. People used stars and constellations for navigation in almost the same way he remembered, yet there did not seem to be any proper body of knowledge about planets beyond the one he was currently living on. Optical tools were also extremely rare in this world, to the point that even owning something like glasses or a ship telescope was already considered a luxury, which meant that building something like a real observatory for serious celestial study could easily become a discovery important enough to change the world itself.

Even with all of that in mind, Elrond still chose to move carefully and not rush anything. He had no desire to follow the exact same road he walked in his previous life, especially not after seeing where that road had led him in the end. Because of that, he decided that this time he would learn through observation, practice, and careful thought while always measuring how much of this world truly matched the one he had once left behind.

After witnessing that little fight between Leon and Lisoletelle, Elrond could not resist teasing Leon a little. The two of them looked strangely compatible when they argued, probably because they had known each other for so long and could throw words at each other without needing to think too hard. Leon looked annoyed, but that only made the whole thing easier to poke at.

"You two look pretty compatible, Leon," Elrond said with a faint grin as he leaned closer to him.

"Huh? Me? Compatible with that girl? No way," Leon replied with clear displeasure on his face. His mouth twisted as if Elrond had just said something insulting, though the reaction only made him look guiltier. Elrond almost laughed at that, but he held it in because Leon already looked close to arguing again.

Unfortunately, Lisoletelle overheard the comment. With her naturally sharp senses, especially her hearing, she caught the whole thing even from her seat. She turned toward Elrond with an angry look and raised her fist at him, making it clear that she had heard more than enough.

"She overheard me," Elrond muttered as he looked away from Lisoletelle's raised fist.

"Of course," Leon said as if that much should have been obvious. "She's really good at hearing." His expression still looked annoyed, but there was no surprise in it at all, which told Elrond that this kind of thing happened often between them.

Cestina laughed at the exchange from the girls' side, soft enough that it did not disturb the whole classroom but clear enough for Elrond to notice. Emilia, however, showed no reaction at all. She sat with the same cool expression, and that lack of response left Elrond with a strange uneasy feeling, so he rested his chin on his arm and watched her for a moment while trying to figure out what was going on with her.

That moment did not last long. The teacher entered the classroom soon after, and the room settled into class as usual. Elrond turned his attention forward, listened to the lesson, and memorized everything written on the board without taking notes because most of his notes were already stored inside his head.

The first class, second class, and third class passed quickly. By lunch break, Elrond would usually eat with Leon and Eiden, but today he had another reason to move. Since Gilbert had assigned him to watch over Emilia, Elrond asked Leon and Eiden to come with him to wherever Emilia ate lunch, making it look like nothing had changed while giving himself a reason to stay nearby.

Apparently, even though Emilia was high nobility, she still ate in the student cafeteria like everyone else. She sat with Cestina, Lisoletelle, and Claire, and the four of them blended into the usual lunch crowd better than Elrond had expected. In practice, his daily academy life did not change much, except that his eyes became more attentive whenever Emilia moved.

Elrond kept doing that for the next several days. Nothing happened, and everything went smoothly enough that Leon and Eiden had no reason to question his lunch choices. Even after days of quiet observation, though, nothing improved between Elrond and Emilia, and the distance between them stayed stale, just like it had been at the beginning.

Sometimes, inside the mansion or at the academy, Elrond tried to start a conversation with her. Each attempt ended almost the same way, with Emilia answering in a short tone or showing little interest, then letting silence swallow the rest. Elrond never pushed too far because forcing the issue would only make him look worse, so he stayed careful and kept acting as a watcher without letting Emilia notice.

Then, during one free period, Emilia left the classroom and went toward the academy garden. Elrond noticed immediately, because by then checking her movements had already become part of his routine. Not long after, he left the classroom too, keeping enough distance to avoid looking like he was following her.

Leon noticed that too. Something about Elrond's behavior had felt off for days, and this time his curiosity finally won. He followed Elrond quietly, keeping enough space between them so Elrond would not notice him right away.

Elrond found Emilia sitting on a garden bench with a botany book open in her hands. She looked absorbed in the pages, her posture neat and still, and for a moment she seemed easier to approach than she ever did in class. Even so, Elrond decided against walking up to her because he was supposed to watch over her, not make the situation more awkward.

He searched for a place where he could observe without standing out. The upper rooftop looked perfect because it had a clear view of the garden and enough distance to keep him from drawing attention. With that decided, he headed up, unaware that Leon was still following him from behind.

Leon followed him again, still quiet. When he saw Elrond heading toward the rooftop, the pieces clicked into place faster than he expected. That rooftop was one of Leon's favorite places in the academy, so seeing Elrond choose it made the whole thing feel even more suspicious.

When Elrond reached the rooftop balcony, he leaned against the railing and looked down toward the garden. He glanced at Emilia now and then, thinking about what he should do next about their strained relationship. He rested his chin on the railing, staring over the academy from the highest point while his thoughts circled around the same problem.

Then Leon tapped him on the back.

"Yo!" Leon said from behind him.

Elrond flinched and turned around fast enough that his sleeve brushed against the railing. "Oh, it's you, Leon. You startled me." He forced his face back into a calm look, though it was already too late to pretend he had not reacted.

"What are you doing up here, Elrond?" Leon asked as he stepped beside him.

"Nothing. Just getting some fresh air," Elrond replied while trying to sound casual. He kept his eyes away from the garden this time, but that only made the answer worse. Leon leaned onto the railing too and looked down, following the direction Elrond had been watching.

"Is that Emilia Alfrost?" Leon asked.

"Where?" Elrond replied, pretending not to know.

"Don't be silly," Leon said as he stared at him with a flat look. "You've been watching her this whole time. I noticed it days ago." His tone carried enough teasing to annoy Elrond, but the sharpness in his eyes made it clear he was not guessing anymore.

"W-What are you talking about?" Elrond said, still trying to hide it as he turned his face away after glancing at Emilia again.

"Well, I don't know why you're hiding it from me," Leon said, letting the teasing grow on purpose. "But I'd assume you're creeping on her, or you're interested in her?" He watched Elrond's face while saying it, clearly waiting for the reaction more than the answer.

"No, it's not like that. I'm not trying to be a creep," Elrond said before stopping mid-sentence. The moment the words left his mouth, he realized what he had done. Denying that specific accusation had already given Leon enough proof.

"Haha... you fell for it," Leon said with a satisfied grin. "So you really are watching her." He looked far too pleased with himself, and Elrond had to admit that Leon had caught him cleanly.

Elrond thought for a moment while looking back down at the garden. Leon was his closest friend at the academy, and hiding everything from him would only make the situation harder if he kept noticing things anyway. After a small exhale, Elrond decided it was better to tell him enough of the truth.

"Alright, alright. You caught me," Elrond said, giving up on the act. "But I swear it's not something creepy, and I'm not interested in her like that." He then explained the situation in a quieter voice, telling Leon about his role as the Alfrost family's guardian and the task Gilbert had given him to watch over Emilia at the academy.

"I see," Leon said after listening without interrupting. "That explains why you've been coming to class late. You live at the Alfrost mansion now." He said it like he had just solved the final piece of a puzzle, and Elrond answered only with a small nod.

Then Elrond looked back down and saw Emilia close her botany book. She stood from the bench and began walking away from the garden, so Elrond moved immediately and left the rooftop without waiting. Leon followed after him, and Elrond did not stop him because having Leon nearby made him look less suspicious, less like a creep following Emilia around alone.

The last time slot came, and as usual, Elrond went to train with Julian. Every time they had a bout, Elrond showed clear improvement, but he still could not reach Julian’s level. Julian had a lot of real combat experience, and even when he held back, he still handled Elrond without much trouble because experience like that could not be faked.

Even so, Julian also did not seem to fully realize that he was improving too. Every time Elrond adapted to one technique, Julian had to change his approach and use something different to stay ahead. In other words, Elrond was not only learning from Julian, but also forcing Julian to refine himself during their fights.

"You're improving a lot, Elrond," Julian said after winning the final bout.

"Thank you. It's thanks to you for showing me new techniques every time," Elrond replied respectfully.

"All I can do is show you what I can," Julian said before pausing for a moment. "...And perhaps you help me as well, since I keep switching my techniques just to beat you. Fighting you has been one of the best exercises I've had lately."

Elrond looked surprised when he heard that. He had never really thought that someone like Julian could benefit from fighting him. To Elrond, Julian was still far above him, so hearing that he was helping Julian improve felt strange, but also a little encouraging.

"Is that so? Then I'm honored," Elrond said. "But I still feel like I'm never catching up with you."

"My late teacher once said you can't overcome someone who grows alongside you," Julian said in a vague way.

At first, the line sounded like a simple motivational saying. But the more Elrond thought about it, the more it started to make sense. If Julian kept growing while Elrond tried to catch up, then simply training with Julian would never be enough to surpass him.

"Does that mean I need to learn somewhere else in order to overcome you, Teach Julian?" Elrond asked after thinking it through, and his conclusion was surprisingly sharp.

"Exactly," Julian replied. "You already have what you need to beat me. And I no longer have anything new to teach you. So you need to piece it together by yourself."

"I see. I'll keep that in mind. Thank you," Elrond said.

A brief silence followed after that as the two of them tidied up the training room. Elrond returned the wooden sword to the rack, while Julian checked the practice area and put everything back where it belonged. The room felt quiet now that the bout was over, with only the sounds of their movements filling the space.

"By the way, how is your job at the Alfrost household?" Julian asked while they continued tidying up.

"Well... a lot of things have happened," Elrond replied.

He thought it over for a moment. Julian was close to the Alfrost family, and as their teacher, he had probably heard some of it already from Emilia or Gilbert. Because of that, Elrond decided that it should be fine to explain the situation to him.

"Actually..." Elrond began.

After that, Elrond explained what had happened. He told Julian about his role in the Alfrost household, his tasks, the awkwardness with Emilia, and the assignment Gilbert had given him to watch over her at the academy. He did not explain everything in perfect detail, but he said enough for Julian to understand the situation.

"I see," Julian said after listening to him. "That sounds complicated. But I believe you'll think it through. Emilia is sharp, and she tends to hide her real emotions sometimes. She's good at it. Consider that advice."

Hearing that, Elrond felt something click in his mind. It explained too much about the way Emilia had been acting around him lately. Maybe she was hiding a grudge or some kind of feeling she refused to show openly.

"Oh... if you're supposed to watch over Emilia, does that mean you aren't doing it right now?" Julian asked. "Is that okay?"

"About that... I thought about it earlier," Elrond said. "But I don't think it's a problem. I can't watch her all the time, and she should be safe with the others right now."

"I see. That's good to hear, then," Julian replied.

After that, they finished tidying up the training room. Julian placed the last item back in its proper place, and Elrond made sure he had not left anything behind. Once everything was done, the two of them parted ways.

#### Scene 2

Sunlight pierced through the shiny glass of the Arbalest Palace, spreading pale reflections across the room as the light shifted over the polished floor and the desk. A man sat behind that desk with a tense and serious expression, resting his cheek against his fist while listening to the plan being presented to him. His sharp gaze made it clear he was not fully convinced, and the atmosphere around him felt heavy with caution.

It was Darius, the second prince of Althania.

"Are you sure?" Darius said with a sharp look in his eyes. "Do you even understand what you're trying to do here? You failed once, didn't you?"

"We did," the man replied without losing his calm. "But that was an abrupt approach. This time, we'll make sure it goes smoothly, and she will be on our side."

As the light shifted again, the man's face became clearer. It was Joren Caldra, standing in front of Darius with his usual polite and composed expression. He did not look nervous at all, even though the topic they were discussing was dangerous enough that one mistake could drag the Second Prince Faction into serious trouble.

"Just remember, don't drag me into this," Darius said as he stood from his seat. He walked toward the door without waiting for a longer explanation, because he had already made his position clear enough. He wanted the result, but he did not want his name attached to the method.

"No need to worry, Lord Darius," Joren said politely after him. "I won't even put my name on it."

The truth of Vow Authority went deeper than simple obedience. Joren had already bound all of his underlings with a condition that made it impossible for them to reveal their master's identity, no matter what happened to them. Even if someone used mind manipulation or mind reading, they would never be able to dig up the name, and if the vow was somehow violated, the mind and soul of the person bound by it would perish instantly, leaving no trace of the true culprit behind them.

Joren stood alone in the room after Darius left, his polite expression unchanged. Then, without moving his lips, he reached out through the vow connection and transmitted his order through thought. The command traveled silently, reaching the person waiting for his instruction.

"Proceed with the plan," Joren transmitted through his thoughts to Mirelle Veyra.

"Understood, as you wish, my Lord," Mirelle Veyra replied in kind.

#### Scene 3

Elrond’s daily routine had become more stagnant after everything that had happened recently. Classes passed like usual, meals happened like usual, and training kept going like usual, but his relationship with Emilia still did not move anywhere. Over the past several days, he tried to understand her feelings through every interaction he had with her, yet nothing seemed to work.

He still could not figure out what was wrong. Every time he tried to speak with her, the conversation ended before it could properly begin, and every time she looked away from him, he was left with another question instead of an answer. Julian’s advice stayed in his head too, because if Emilia was really good at hiding her true feelings, then her cold attitude might not be as simple as it looked.

Because of that, Elrond started revisiting every memory he had of her. He began from their first meeting back in his hometown when he was seven, but that had been nothing more than a first encounter from what he remembered. Nothing meaningful happened then, unless something had happened outside his awareness, and that possibility bothered him because he could remember the scene clearly but still could not know what Emilia had felt.

Then there was their second encounter, when he saved her. Even now, Elrond could not recall doing anything wrong in that situation. All he did was save them, and yet the way Emilia acted around him now made the question circle in his mind again and again.

Maybe he had done something he should not have done. Maybe it was something small, something he failed to notice at the time because he had been focused on danger and survival. Or maybe he had not done anything wrong at all, and Emilia’s coldness had nothing to do with him.

If that was the case, then it would be the best scenario. If Emilia truly held no grudge against him, then at least he was not the source of the problem. It would still mean there was something he did not understand, but that was better than knowing he had hurt her without realizing it.
